searchText: <@301186049323958275> you're going in a bizarre direction regarding what is and is not under consensus. It's not clear to me what problem it solves or what the underlying theory is <@332923501079953409> Which idea is this in response to? Pretty much everything you say about 1559 has this property. You mean https://discordapp.com/channels/595666850260713488/692078615269212180/718613679775678504 ? Yes, that especially. I haven't thought through that idea thoroughly, feel free to rip it apart. 😄 It feels like a moderately huge philosophical shift that removes the end users How so? ...ability to predict what will happen from block to block How so? They lose the ability to predict block sizes, but that should be it? Miners publish blocks of whatever size they want, knowing that the bigger their block, the more likely it is to be uncled and we let that alone be the downward pressure on block size. practically people need to know that limit because many smart contract deployments are at or beyond the block size limit. Ah, you mean you think there is value in having a *minimum* block size? Yes. There already are miners with a *functionally* small block size. That is, there are miners who publish non-full blocks during times of "congestion". So users *already* don't have that guarantee. and no upper bound is ultimately centralizing along the axis of dark fiber. That is a strong argument, that miner conglomerates on a high performance closed network would outperform miners outside of that closed network. I think the miner games are broken, so I'm not going to disagree about that, it just seems like you're moving in the direction of "break them more, it will net out better" which i don't entirely disagree with but i find it a lot harder to model than you seem to 😄 I also think we need to do a lot more modeling to fix the miner games, or we should you know, move more aggressively to PoS, which has a completely different set of games. Meh, I'm not in a huge hurry for either PoS or my brainstorm proposal above. I think the system is close enough to equilibrium *at the moment* that I'm not worried about it breaking short term, and long term I think PoS will eventually replace it so I'm satisfied with the long term outlook being kinda fuzzy. I would be much more concerned if I was a Bitcoin developer recognizing that we had no plan for addressing the eventual termination of block rewards. 😄 Yeah, it's kinda safe to assume that Satoshi didn't worry about because he thought he'd be dead and was right 😄 The idea of well connected miners being rewarded better than poorly connected miners is interesting. I think we have that problem already though? A well connected miner is less likely to be uncled than a poorly connected miner at the moment. We already have that problem and pretend we don't. blocks come from a particular set of ASNs... So poorly connected miners are incentivized to mine smaller blocks (or more specifically, demand a higher min price), which means their reward per watt is lower. it's not even remotely well distributed across the internet.
